newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedes slightly more gloomy on economy - survey.
newsitem.headline: Swedes slightly more gloomy on economy - survey.

text.p: Swedish households have become somewhat more pessimistic about the economy, a survey by Statistics Sweden showed on Monday.

The proportion of households expecting the economy to worsen rose to 33 percent in September from 31 percent in August, whilst those expecting it to improve over the next 12 months rose to 22 percent from 21 percent.

Figures on household economies were steady, with 18 percent of the sample expecting harder times and the same amount seeing an improvement. These two figures were the same at the time of the last poll one month ago.
The households surveyed believed inflation would rise 1.6 percent in the coming 12 months, compared to a rise of 1.7 percent forecast a month ago.
The survey had 52 percent forecasting a higher jobless rate compared to 53 percent a month earlier, and 12 percent expecting lower unemployment, the same as in August.
